title: fix(plugin-approvals): the decision that ends an approval tells its submitter the outcome
body:
Fixes #24753

Clause-②: yes

## What this changes

Approving or rejecting a request notified nobody. A send-back (`approval.returned`) and a question (`approval.request_info`) reached the submitter; the decision did not. Now `ApprovalService.decide()` tells the submitter the outcome once the decision ends the approval process:

- **Topics:** `approval.approved` ("Request approved") and `approval.rejected` ("Request rejected"), one per outcome.
- **Shape:** the same as the sibling notices. It goes to the request's own `submitter_id`. The record is named by `nameSubjectRecord`, the label-and-id rule from #23556 (`Your Deal D_123 was rejected.`). The body is never empty, the rule from #21847. When the decider wrote a comment, it follows the sentence as its own paragraph. `notify()` deep-links the notice to `/system/approvals?request=ID`. The actor is the person the decision's context vouches for. The organization is the request's.
- **Who is not told:**
  - a submitter who decided their own request;
  - anyone, on a co-sign vote that leaves the request pending;
  - anyone, when the resume opened a further approval step on the same run;
  - anyone, for the SLA sweep's `auto_approve` / `auto_reject`. The escalation's own submitter notice (`approval.sla_breached`, which names the action) remains the one message, so `notifySubmitter: false` still silences it. The sweep now calls a private `decideAndResume(..., 'escalation')`. The public `decide()` delegates to the same method with `'outcome'`.
- **Docs:** a new callout in `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`. The old advice to "keep notify nodes that report the decision" is narrowed to recipients other than the submitter.
- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` `minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. *(Seat edit: the declaration was re-made by the seat, claim amendment 6286428768, to match this lane's precedent #22607, which shipped the new `approval.requested` topic as `yes (widening)` and `minor`. The dev's patch round at `0110fecb03` moved the changeset; this line and line 3 are the seat's.)*

## Readings taken before writing it (origin/main a43405d596)

- **H1 holds.** The send-back paths send `approval.returned` (in `sendBack`, both the revision-limit auto-reject and the plain send-back), `requestInfo` sends `approval.request_info`, and `escalateRequest` notifies the submitter under `esc.notifySubmitter !== false`. All of them address `raw.submitter_id` and use the closed `{ title, body, actionUrl }` payload. No approval `notify()` call site reads the caller's locale; every body is one English sentence.
- **H2, refined.** The status write for approve and reject is shared, in `decideNode`'s finalizing branch. The notice cannot be sent there, because only the resume in `decide()` shows whether the run moved on to another approval step. So the notice sits in `decide()`, after the resume. This also means a decision whose resume strands sends no notice, the same as a send-back in that state.
- **No registry is needed.** `service-messaging` has no topic registry. `PreferenceResolver` matches the exact topic or `*` (default on, fail-open), so the new topics are picked up with no wiring, and a user can mute one outcome and keep the other. objectui (local checkout 90518cd) groups inbox arrivals by `type` generically and holds no approval topic list.

## Tests

Measured at head 2a13930f15.

- New `approval-decision-outcome-notification.integration.test.ts`, 8 cases. It uses the real `ApprovalService` on a real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3 in memory), with the real `AutomationEngine` running the flows and the real approval node opening each step. The cases:
  - approved;
  - rejected with a comment;
  - self-decided, with a control;
  - a unanimous co-sign;
  - a two-step ladder;
  - a rejection at step one;
  - a decision gateway that skips the second step;
  - an SLA auto-approve under `notifySubmitter` true and false, with a human-decision control.
- `approval-notification-body.integration.test.ts`: the battery drives the new call site, so its "every call site" claim still holds (now thirteen of fourteen). The body, record-name and organization pins cover both new topics.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals test`: 87 files, 1155 tests passed. `typecheck`: exit 0, and `check:test-typecheck` is OK with the new file unledgered and error-free.
- **Ablations.** Each leg used `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which checks the anchor (1 to 0 hits), checks that the blob changed, and restores with `git checkout HEAD -- ABS_PATH`. Each restore was proven: blob equals HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
  - Dropping the `notifyDecisionOutcome` call: 11 tests red across both files, including every negative case through its positive control.
  - Removing the self-decider guard: only the self-decided test is red.
  - Removing the next-step guard: only the two-step test is red.
  - Passing `'outcome'` from the SLA sweep: only the SLA test is red.

## Gates (local subset)

All of these were run at head 2a13930f15. Each exit code was captured before any pipe.

- **Derived list.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 98 commands from the 5-path diff. All 98 exited 0.
- **Reconciliation.** `--ran` (with `:: exit N` records) answered: 98 derived, 98 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, a derived zero.
- **First pass, at 9827a640fb.** Three gates stopped with PREREQUISITE NOT MET (exit 3), so they measured nothing: `check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n`. I built their prerequisites and re-ran them; all three exited 0. `check:query-options-erasure` was red (exit 1), because the new test file's two query-option bags were erased with an `any` cast (test surface 236 to 238). It is green at 236 since commit 2a13930f15, which types them (`satisfies EngineQueryOptions`).
- **Not run locally.** `test:repo` is not run here; this diff touches none of its tests, so it is left to CI. The full-battery dogfood pin (`approval-notification-body.dogfood.test.ts`) is also left to CI. The CI families are left to the PR's own check-runs.

## Acceptance notes

- **Who a multi-step notice reaches.** A later approval step's request records the PREVIOUS step's decider as its `submitter_id`. Measured: on a manager-then-executive flow, step 1 holds `u_sub` and step 2 holds `u_mgr`. The cause is that `approval-node.ts` passes `context.userId` as `submitterId`, and the resume-as-decider hand-off has switched that to the decider. So on a multi-step flow the final notice reaches that person, as step 2's send-back, request-info and SLA submitter notices already do. The pin asserts the notice follows the terminal request's stored `submitter_id`, so it stays green whichever person that field ends up naming. Reported to the seat as a finding and left unchanged here: it is outside this card's file surface and is a different defect.
- **The revision-limit auto-reject keeps its old topic.** It still tells the submitter on `approval.returned` ("Approval auto-rejected"), not on `approval.rejected`. Unchanged here.
- **Subflow boundary.** The "is there a next step" read covers the request's own run. If an approval inside a subflow is followed by another approval in the parent run, the notice is sent at the child's decision. This case was not measured.
- **The action-link comment.** A decision through the action link records the comment "Via action link", and the outcome notice carries it as the comment paragraph.
- **No resend after repair.** A decision whose resume strands sends no notice, and the operator repair path (`continueRestoredRun`) does not send one later.

## Out of scope

#22607 is the precedent for adding an approval topic. It is referenced, not touched. #23556 and #21847 are the families whose rules this notice follows.
